pins.definition: To move something such as a door or lid so that an opening is covered, or to bring parts together.
To shut something such as a door, window, or one's eyes, or to stop being open to the public.
To move something so that an opening, door, or container is no longer open, or to stop a business from operating.

situation: A shopkeeper at dusk pulls down a heavy slatted metal security shutter over a storefront window.
subject: the shutting of an opening
brief: A shopkeeper's hands pull downward on the bottom handle of a corrugated metal storefront shutter, lowering it halfway across a brightly lit display window to cover the opening. The lower half of the glass is now dark behind the grey metal slats while the upper half still shows the warm interior.
prompt: A shopkeeper's hands pull downward on the bottom handle of a corrugated metal storefront shutter, lowering it halfway across a brightly lit display window to cover the opening. The lower half of the glass is now dark behind the grey metal slats while the upper half still shows the warm interior. a mid-century travel poster painted in gouache, rich opaque colour, confident simplified forms with real painted texture, strong diagonal composition. One square illustration. The scene is fully rendered and fully inhabited — no silhouettes, no flat icons, no diagram, no empty schematic space. A single subject dominates the frame and everything else is arranged around it. Absolutely no text anywhere in the image: no letters, words, numbers, captions, labels, signage, logos, watermarks or pseudo-text.
